title: Device-Code Phishing
overview: Inspect device-flow sign-in records for successful use on an app outside an expected device policy.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and entra sign-in or audit projection fields.

attack.name: Spearphishing Link
attack.rationale: T1566.002 represents link-based phishing delivery that can lead to a device grant. The fixture observes the grant only.

hypothesis: An unmanaged device-flow grant to an unapproved application merits checking user intent and policy.
evidence: Locate application ID, flow type, device posture and user, then review follow-on token use by that application.
false_positive: Headless device onboarding and some administrator tools legitimately use device flow.
tuning: Constrain allowed applications and devices, and sample approved flows to make narrow exceptions.
response: Confirm the user initiated the action, revoke suspicious sessions and review the associated application activity.
prevention: Limit device authorization flow to approved applications with conditional access and user education.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The grant may reflect abuse without showing the delivery mechanism. No codes or tokens are present.

questions.prompt: What provides context beyond the flow type?
options: The size of the sign-in table
questions.explanation: Device flow is legitimate for some applications. Context identifies unexpected use.

questions.prompt: What should you ask the account owner?
options: Whether they know the event ID by heart
Whether they initiated the device authorization
questions.explanation: User intent helps distinguish phishing from a sanctioned grant.
